title: The Hedge Fund That Paid Meteorologists to Fake Hurricane Warnings
hook: They didn't just predict the storm — they manufactured it on paper to crash insurance stocks and pocket millions.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines natural disaster fear with white-collar crime — viewers love seeing how the rich cheat the system.

title: The Startup That Sold AI Tutors—They Were Laos Prisoners on Headsets
hook: 'Powered by AI' meant a room of inmates reading from scripts, paid in cigarettes, and flagged as 'offshore talent.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Horror + irony — the startup marketed 'revolutionary AI education' while running a prison sweatshop.

title: The Monopoly That Bought Every Grain Silo—Then Let Farmers Starve
hook: They owned the storage, set the prices, and when farmers refused to sell cheap, they left the crops to rot.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into food insecurity fears and anti-corporate anger — everyone eats, everyone cares.

title: The Trader Who Used a Fake 'Tsunami' Report to Dump Shipping Stocks
hook: He paid a radio station intern to air a 'breaking news' alert — and sold $40 million in shares before anyone checked the ocean.
why_this_can_go_viral: Shows how fragile markets are to fake news — and the audacity of using a natural disaster to cheat.

title: The Dark Marketing Agency That Used Baby Monitors to Listen for Arguments
hook: They hacked infant audio feeds, detected marital fights, and served divorce lawyer ads before the couple made up.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme privacy violation — the idea that a baby monitor could weaponize your family disputes is nightmare fuel.

title: The Trader Who Faked a 'Central Bank Leak' to Crash a Currency
hook: He forged an internal memo, leaked it to Bloomberg, and tanked the peso before anyone realized the signature was wrong.
why_this_can_go_viral: Shows how easily global markets can be fooled by a single forged document — David vs. Goliath energy.
